cards.title: TypeSafe AI Launches Jev: A Non-Autoregressive 'System One' Model for Structured Decisions
cards.why_it_matters: A former OpenAI researcher is releasing a new model class with a new architecture, parallel sampler, and training method (RLCD) explicitly targeting structured automation—a genuine architectural departure worth tracking.
cards.summary: TypeSafe AI (founded by ex-OpenAI researcher Diogo Almeida) releases Jev, a frontier model that outputs all probabilities in parallel rather than autoregressively generating tokens. It targets structured, typed outputs only—no string generation, no hallucination by construction. Claims two orders of magnitude faster and more efficient than LLMs on 'System One' tasks, using a training method called Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions (RLCD). Benchmarked against Astra and Fable as reference models.

cards.title: Tokeniser Search Procedure Beats Objective: BPE's Bottom-Up Merging Is the Key Factor
cards.why_it_matters: If you train or fine-tune LMs and care about tokenisation choices, this gives you a principled, experimentally grounded answer to a long-standing confound between BPE and UnigramLM.
cards.summary: By completing a 2×2 design space (objective × search), the authors isolate that bottom-up search—not compression vs. log-likelihood objective—dominates bits-per-byte performance across model sizes, vocabulary sizes, and English/multilingual settings. BLiMP grammaticality scores, however, show no consistent relationship with either design axis.

cards.title: ComPO: Zeroth-Order Preference Alignment Mitigates Likelihood Displacement
cards.why_it_matters: As a researcher working with RLHF and post-training, this offers a theoretically grounded alternative to DPO-style methods with convergence guarantees and empirical wins on Llama, Gemma, and Qwen3.
cards.summary: ComPO uses comparison oracles to extract directional gradient information from preference pairs without optimizing a differentiable loss, sidestepping likelihood displacement. An online variant adds reverse-KL control via unlabeled policy generations. Experiments on Mistral, Llama, Gemma-2, Qwen3, and Gemma-3 show improved length-controlled win rates over existing direct alignment methods.

cards.title: History-Dependent Logging Causes Exponential Sample Complexity in Off-Policy Evaluation
cards.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to RL and offline RL researchers: shows that standard coverage conditions are insufficient when the logger uses history, with a tight theoretical lower bound and matching estimator.
cards.summary: For any horizon H≥3, the authors construct POMDPs with at most two latent states per stage where action coverage, belief coverage, and behavior-marginal outcome-revealing conditions all hold with constants independent of H, yet evaluating a known deterministic target policy to accuracy 1/8 requires Θ((3/2)^H log(1/δ)) episodes. The hardness mechanism is a reset that erases the unknown transition determining target value; a matching optimal estimator is also derived.

cards.title: ScienceIDE Turns Scientific Code Repositories into RL/SFT Training Environments for Agents
cards.why_it_matters: For researchers building code agents or studying transfer learning, this infrastructure converts real scientific codebases into verifiable training environments with evidence of positive transfer to general benchmarks.
cards.summary: ScienceIDE wraps scientific repositories into programmable environments with expert-defined acceptance criteria, supporting task generation, execution, and verification for SFT, RL, and eval. Models trained on verified trajectories—PhAI-IDE-72B, 9B, and 4B—show gains on held-out scientific code repair and selected general-purpose code, reasoning, and knowledge benchmarks.

cards.title: PANORAMA: Panoptic Grounded Captioning with Pixel-Level Mask Selection
cards.why_it_matters: Relevant for researchers building vision-language agents that need both detailed captions and spatially precise grounding—this provides a new benchmark, metric, and model tackling both simultaneously.
cards.summary: PANORAMA frames phrase grounding as mask proposal selection conditioned on contextualized phrase representations, jointly trained with caption generation. The authors introduce PanoCaps (human-annotated, near-complete pixel coverage) and a generalized Panoptic Quality metric. PANORAMA achieves best overall grounding on PanoCaps and matches or exceeds specialized models on several pixel-level grounding tasks.

cards.title: Audio-Augmented Video Generation Gives Robots Force Profiles for Contact-Rich Manipulation
cards.why_it_matters: Bridges a concrete gap in robot learning from video—force information—using generated audio loudness as a proxy signal, a novel multimodal angle relevant to embodied AI researchers.
cards.summary: The pipeline generates both video and contact audio from natural-language prompts, deriving kinematic trajectories and time-varying desired-force profiles from audio loudness. A closed-loop force regulator on a Franka Panda robot tracks these profiles during contact. The approach succeeds on contact-rich tasks where kinematic-only baselines fail, and is also used as a data engine for policy training.
